clinician.trajectory_summary: A 44-year-old previously healthy Chinese man with no prior varicella history and no immunosuppression presented with a 5-day history of vesicular eruption. Clinical examination revealed two distinct but concurrent presentations: (1) small vesicles (1-2 mm diameter) surrounded by erythema on the trunk, back, and neck, clinically diagnosed as varicella; and (2) papules and vesicles in ribbons on the left ear involving 1-3 dermatomes with unilateral distribution and ulcerated lesions, clinically diagnosed as herpes zoster. Vesicular fluids were collected from both varicella and herpes zoster lesions. Nested PCR detected only VZV (HSV-1 and HSV-2 ruled out). Phylogenetic analysis of 6 ORFs (ORFs 1, 21, 22, 50, 54, and 68) identified VZV genotype J (clade 2) from both the trunk and head lesions. The patient was treated with valacyclovir, ebastine, mecobalamine, pregabalin, and calamine lotion. Lesions crusted and completely resolved within 1 week of treatment. This case represents a rare occurrence of concurrent varicella and herpes zoster caused by the same VZV genotype J in an immunocompetent host.
